task1.title: Liverton Docks redevelopment
task1.prompt: The diagram shows how Liverton Docks have changed since 1980.

chartDesc.title: Liverton Docks
changes: Top-left warehouse replaced by education centre
Top cranes and second warehouse removed and replaced/added with sailing club and kid's playground
Commercial ships replaced by a Ship Museum
Bridge and Flood Barrier constructed across the river
Bottom-left crane replaced by a Hotel
Bottom warehouse area converted into Apartments
Parking built to the east of Apartments
River walk added along the southern side of the river
chartDesc.overview: From 1980 to the present, Liverton Docks was completely transformed from an industrial commercial port featuring warehouses, cranes, and working ships into a recreational, educational, and residential area.
keyFeatures: Removal of industrial facilities (warehouses and cranes)
Addition of educational and leisure facilities (education centre, sailing club, kid's playground, Ship Museum)
Addition of residential and commercial features (Hotel, Apartments, parking, River walk)
Infrastructure developments across the river (bridge, Flood Barrier)

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparison where relevant.

The diagram shows the changes in Liverton Docks from 1980 to now.

In 1980, there was a port and some warehouses. There was also a road and some land next to the water. The port was used for boats. After that, things changed a lot. The port is now gone.

The warehouses were changed into apartments. The road is still there. There is now a hotel and a shopping centre where the land was. Also there is a carpark. The apartments are near the water. The shopping center is next to the apartments. The hotel is near the road and carpark. It is a very different place now.

So, the docks are now a place for people to live and shop and stay in a hotel. There is no port anymore.

The diagram shows how Liverton Docks has changed between 1980 and today. Overall, the docks have been redeveloped, with industry being replaced by areas for leisure and housing.

In 1980, the docks were mainly industrial. There were large warehouses along the north side, and a shipyard in the south-east corner. A road ran along the west side. Today, the warehouses have been demolished and replaced with apartments. In addition to this, the shipyard has been removed and a leisure centre has been built in its place. It is also noticeable that a car park has been constructed next to the leisure centre. The road remains in the same place, however, a roundabout has been added at the north end.

Furthermore, the area to the east of the docks has also been transformed. Previously, this area was used for industry, but now it contains a marina and a shopping centre. The changes suggest a shift from industry to residential and recreational use.

task2.title: International news in schools
task2.prompt: Some people think secondary school students should study international news as one of their subjects, while others believe that this is a waste of valuable school time. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
task2.instruction: Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
task2.sampleBand5:
Some people think that high school students should learn about international news in school. Other people think it is not a good idea and it is waste of time. This essay will talk about both sides of the argument and give my opinion.

On the one hand, learning about international news is important for students. They can learn about what is happening in the world. For example, they can learn about wars and natural disasters. This can help them to become more better citizens and understand different cultures. Also, if students know about international news, they can be more prepared for the future. Maybe they will work in a job that involves international relations, or they might travel to other countries.

However, other people think that international news is not important for high school students. They think that students should focus on other subjects, like math and science. These subjects are more important for getting a job. Also, some people think that international news is too complicated for high school students to understand. It can confuse them and make them feel worried about the world.

In my opinion, I think that high school students should learn about international news, but it should not take up too much time. It should be part of a class, like social studies, and the teacher should explain the news in a way that is easy to understand. Like, they should make it fun. This way, students can learn about the world without feeling overwhelmed.
task2.sampleBand6:
There is a debate about whether or not secondary school students should study international news as part of their curriculum. Some people think it is a good idea, while others believe it is not a good use of time. This essay will discuss both sides of this argument and then give my own opinion.

On the one hand, there are several reasons why studying international news could be beneficial. Firstly, it can help students to become more aware of different cultures and perspectives. This is important in today's globalized world, where people from different countries are increasingly interacting with each other. Secondly, understanding international news can help students develop critical thinking skills. They can learn to analyze information from different sources and form their own opinions. Finally, knowing about current events around the world can make students more engaged citizens who are better equipped to participate in discussions about important global issues.

However, there are also arguments against including international news in the school curriculum. One common argument is that secondary school students already have a lot to learn, and adding another subject would put too much pressure on them. Also, some people might say that international news is not as important as other subjects, such as math or science, which are essential for future careers. It could be argued that school time is better spent on these core subjects. Furthermore, some teachers might not feel qualified to teach international news, which could lead to students receiving inaccurate or biased information.

In my opinion, while there are valid concerns about adding international news to the curriculum, the benefits outweigh the drawbacks. Schools could consider incorporating international news into existing subjects like history or social studies, rather than creating a separate course. Also, teachers can use reliable resources to make sure the information they give is correct and unbiased. Therefore, I think that, with careful planning, studying international news can be a valuable experience for secondary school students, helping them to become more informed and engaged global citizens, even if it requires some changes to the current curriculum.
task2.sampleBand7:
The question of whether secondary school students should study international news as a compulsory subject is a contentious one. While some argue that it is a valuable use of school time, others contend that it is an unnecessary addition to an already crowded curriculum. This essay will explore both perspectives before presenting my own opinion.

Proponents of including international news in the curriculum often argue that it is crucial for fostering global citizenship. By learning about current events in other countries, students can develop a better understanding of different cultures, political systems, and social issues. This, in turn, can help them to become more informed and engaged citizens of the world. Furthermore, studying international news can enhance critical thinking skills as students learn to analyze different perspectives and evaluate sources of information. Some might suggest that this is especially important in today's increasingly interconnected world, where global events can have a significant impact on local communities.

However, there are also valid arguments against making international news a compulsory subject. One common concern is that secondary school curricula are already packed with essential subjects such as mathematics, science, and literature. Adding another subject, particularly one that may be perceived as less directly relevant to future career prospects, could place undue pressure on students. Moreover, some educators might argue that international news is best learned through independent reading and research, rather than through structured classroom lessons. They believe that students should be encouraged to pursue their own interests and learn about the world at their own pace.

In my opinion, while there are benefits to studying international news, making it a compulsory subject is not necessarily the best approach. I believe that schools should instead focus on integrating international perspectives into existing subjects, such as history and social studies. This would allow students to learn about global issues in a more holistic and engaging way, without adding to their workload. Furthermore, schools could offer optional extracurricular activities, such as debate clubs or Model United Nations, for students who are particularly interested in international affairs. This would provide a more flexible and personalized approach to learning about the world. Perhaps it would be useful to assess the current curriculum to identify areas that could be improved.

In conclusion, while understanding international news is undoubtedly important, it is not necessarily essential to make it a compulsory subject in secondary schools. A more integrated and flexible approach, which incorporates global perspectives into existing subjects and offers optional extracurricular activities, may be a more effective way to educate students about the world.
task2.sampleBand8:
The question of whether secondary school students should study international news is a contentious one. While some argue that it is a valuable use of school time, others maintain that it detracts from more essential subjects. This essay will discuss both perspectives before presenting my own opinion.

Proponents of incorporating international news into the curriculum believe that it is crucial for fostering global citizenship. By learning about current events in other countries, students can develop a broader understanding of different cultures, political systems, and economic realities. This exposure can cultivate empathy and critical thinking skills, enabling them to engage with complex global issues in a more informed and nuanced way. Furthermore, knowledge of international affairs is increasingly relevant in today's interconnected world, where economic and political decisions in one country can have far-reaching consequences for others. Students who are conversant with global trends are better prepared to navigate the challenges and opportunities of the 21st century.

Conversely, those who oppose the inclusion of international news argue that secondary school curricula are already overloaded, and that time spent on current events would be better dedicated to core subjects such as mathematics, science, and literature. They contend that these subjects provide students with foundational knowledge and skills that are essential for academic success and future careers. Moreover, some argue that international news can be overwhelming and anxiety-inducing for young people, particularly if it focuses on negative events such as conflicts and disasters. Concerns also exist about the potential for bias in news reporting and the difficulty of presenting complex issues in an objective and balanced manner. A further argument is that families and individuals can pursue international news independently through various media outlets, rendering its inclusion in the school curriculum redundant.

In my opinion, while the concerns about curriculum overload and potential bias are valid, the benefits of studying international news outweigh the drawbacks. Schools can address these concerns by integrating international news into existing subjects, such as history, geography, and social studies, rather than creating a separate course. Furthermore, teachers can play a crucial role in facilitating critical analysis of news sources and encouraging students to consider multiple perspectives. Overall, I believe that equipping students with a solid understanding of global affairs is an essential investment in their future and the future of our world. By carefully curating and contextualizing international news, schools can empower students to become informed, engaged, and responsible global citizens. Striking a balance between core subjects and global awareness is key.

The question of whether international news should be a mandatory subject in secondary schools is a topic of considerable debate. While some argue that it represents a misallocation of valuable educational time, others maintain that it is essential for fostering informed and globally aware citizens. This essay will explore both perspectives before offering my own view.

Proponents of integrating international news into the curriculum often emphasize its role in cultivating global citizenship. In an increasingly interconnected world, understanding international affairs is crucial for comprehending global challenges such as climate change, economic interdependence, and political instability. Exposure to diverse perspectives and cultural contexts can broaden students' horizons, promote empathy, and encourage critical thinking about complex global issues. Furthermore, familiarity with international news can equip students with the knowledge and skills necessary to participate actively in democratic processes and contribute to informed decision-making on issues with international implications. A nuanced understanding of global events can also foster a sense of responsibility towards the global community.

Conversely, opponents argue that dedicating valuable school time to international news is impractical and potentially detrimental to students' academic progress in core subjects. They contend that secondary school curricula are already overloaded with essential subjects such as mathematics, science, and literature. Introducing international news as a mandatory subject could divert resources and attention away from these fundamental areas, potentially hindering students' overall academic performance. Moreover, some argue that the complexities of international news may be overwhelming or even anxiety-inducing for young students, particularly if presented without adequate context or guidance. Concerns are also sometimes raised about the potential for biased or sensationalized reporting, which could distort students' perceptions of global events.

In my opinion, while the concerns raised by opponents are valid, the benefits of incorporating international news into secondary education outweigh the potential drawbacks. Rather than making it a separate, mandatory subject, schools could integrate international news into existing subjects such as history, social studies, or even language arts. This approach would allow students to develop a more holistic understanding of global issues without overburdening the curriculum. Furthermore, teachers can play a crucial role in providing context, facilitating critical analysis, and promoting balanced perspectives. By carefully curating and presenting international news, schools can empower students to become informed, engaged, and responsible global citizens. The key lies in striking a balance between providing students with essential knowledge and fostering critical thinking skills. Given the increasing interconnectedness of our world, equipping students with a solid understanding of international affairs is an investment in their future and the future of our global society.
task2.sampleAnswer:
Whether international news should be incorporated into secondary school curricula is a topic of considerable debate. While some see it as an essential educational component, others view it as an unnecessary distraction. This essay will examine both perspectives before presenting my own view.

Advocates for teaching international news argue that it prepares students for life in an increasingly globalized world. Understanding current events helps young people develop critical thinking skills as they learn to analyze information from various sources and distinguish fact from opinion. Additionally, exposure to global issues can foster empathy and cultural awareness, encouraging students to become informed, responsible citizens. In an age of misinformation, teaching students how to consume news critically is arguably more important than ever.

On the other hand, critics contend that valuable school time should be devoted to core academic subjects that directly contribute to students' future careers and further education. They argue that international news is constantly changing and therefore difficult to examine fairly, and that students can easily access news outside of school hours. Furthermore, there are concerns that teachers might inadvertently introduce political bias when discussing current affairs, potentially influencing students' viewpoints inappropriately.

In my opinion, studying international news should be part of the secondary school curriculum, but as an integrated component rather than a standalone subject. News literacy can be effectively incorporated into existing subjects such as social studies, languages, and media studies. This approach would allow students to develop important analytical skills while also covering essential academic content. The key is to teach students how to evaluate news critically rather than simply presenting current events.
